README.md.content:
# Optional transfer: reconstruct application records

This optional Network Stack activity follows the required transport observation
project. The required project traces a request and compares TCP with UDP. This
transfer asks a different question: how can one application recover several
records when a TCP read returns only part of a record?

The deliverable is a saved case configuration and an evidence notebook. The
supplied Python is instrumentation; programming is optional. The reference
configuration also needs its own observations and explanation.

## Environment and files

Use an ordinary non-root account in an owned Linux environment with Python 3.10
or newer. Check `uname -s`, `hostname`, `pwd`, and `python3 --version` in the
terminal that will run the project. The application refuses other environments.
On macOS select an owned Linux lab through Remote SSH or use a Linux VM. On
Windows use the Linux terminal in WSL. An editor window does not identify the
terminal's execution host. No remote connection is created by this project.

Both roles contain `main.py`, `transport_lab.py`, `case.json`, `network-notes.md`,
and `edge-cases.md`. The shared README explains the investigation. Open
`starter/` for the independent attempt and keep its instrumentation unchanged.

The experiment creates a listener and client on `127.0.0.1` using a port chosen
by the operating system, exchanges only its own data, closes its sockets and
joins its owned worker thread. It changes no routes, firewall, DNS settings, or
system services. Loopback belongs to the current Linux network namespace, so
the reported endpoint cannot be used to infer reachability from another host.

## Distinguish the units

A socket exposes transport operations to an application. TCP provides an
ordered byte stream; it does not add application record boundaries. A successful
read can return fewer bytes than the application needs. An IP packet, a TCP
segment, a send call, a receive call, a Unicode character, and an application
record are different units. The socket observations here do not reveal packet
boundaries. See the primary [Linux TCP manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/tcp.7.html)
and [TCP specification](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html).

This application's record format is four bytes containing an unsigned payload
length in network byte order, followed by that many UTF-8 bytes. The length
counts encoded bytes, rather than the number of displayed characters. Two
records follow one another without an extra separator. The format belongs to
this application; TCP does not invent or interpret it.

The apparatus deliberately sends the first byte of the first length prefix,
waits until the client has read it, and then sends the remainder. This gate
makes the partial observation reproducible without predicting network packet
segmentation or relying on a sleep. The first read asks for two bytes and gets
the one byte currently available. Later read sizes can vary.

For this bounded trial the apparatus drains the stream to EOF and records all
raw reads. The selected application decoder receives either just the first
read or the reconstructed stream. A real application can decode complete
length-prefixed records incrementally; it does not need to wait for a
connection to close. EOF here ends the finite trial. EOF by itself does not
prove that every intended application record was complete.

## Predict, observe, correct

1. Read `case.json` and predict what the selected decoder can learn from a
   one-byte input. Sketch the first four-byte length field before running.
2. In `starter/`, run `python3 main.py --report tcp-first.json`. The report name
   must be new. Exit status 78 means the observed application result does not
   meet the goal; the report still contains the transport observations.
3. Compare `firstReadHex`, the concatenation of `readCalls[*].dataHex`, and
   `wireHex`. The transport can deliver the complete stream even while the
   selected application decoder receives an incomplete prefix. Identify which
   part failed using the report's actual fields.
4. Change only the `framing` setting in `case.json` to select length-prefix
   reconstruction. Keep the first report. Run
   `python3 main.py --report tcp-corrected.json` and explain why each decoded
   record now has a boundary.
5. Predict the alternate message count and the effect of its UTF-8 payload,
   then run `python3 main.py --alternate --report tcp-alternate.json`.
   Compare payload byte lengths with visible character counts. Use that run's
   endpoint, process, thread, and actual read evidence.

Exit status zero checks the apparatus's application contract. It does not
complete `network-notes.md`. Keep predictions, observed command/report names,
the configuration change, a byte-level explanation, and one limitation there.
Use `edge-cases.md` to explain how a decoder handles a partial length,
a partial payload, or an invalid advertised size. Those reasoning cases are
not claims that this trial sent malformed input.

## Inspect and troubleshoot

For an optional syscall view, install `strace` in the selected Linux lab and
run a fresh trial, for example:

    strace -f -yy -s 4096 -e trace=network,close -o tcp-syscalls.txt python3 main.py --report tcp-traced.json

Match file descriptors, loopback endpoints and thread IDs to the report.
`sendall` is a Python operation that can produce one or more kernel sends;
do not assume one Python call equals one packet. The
[Python socket documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/socket.html)
explains the API, and [recv(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/recv.2.html)
documents the Linux receive behavior.

An existing report path is refused so evidence is not replaced. Invalid case
keys or values are refused before the sockets are created. A socket-policy
error or an owned-peer timeout is a local lab failure to inspect, not evidence
of a remote firewall or DNS problem. The finite socket deadlines and cleanup
checks bound each trial. If a run fails, keep its report and command before
trying a new filename in a suitable owned Linux environment.

## Independent and paced checkpoints

Independently, complete the prediction, baseline, correction, alternate and
explanation before consulting `solution/`. In a paced session pause after the
first one-byte observation and ask which layer knows where a record ends.
Resume with the same case and notebook rather than starting another required
project. The separate UDP extension has a different deliverable and its own
attempt.

"""Owned Linux loopback observations for two optional transport investigations."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import socket
import struct
import sys
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path


def stamp():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()  # noqa: UP017


def source_hashes():
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    return {name: hashlib.sha256((root / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            for name in ["main.py", "transport_lab.py", "case.json", "network-notes.md", "edge-cases.md"]}


def identity():
    return {"pid": os.getpid(), "uid": os.getuid(), "hostname": socket.gethostname(),
            "cwd": str(Path.cwd()), "networkNamespace": os.readlink("/proc/self/ns/net"),
            "mountNamespace": os.readlink("/proc/self/ns/mnt")}


class Experiment:
    def __init__(self):
        self.sockets = []
        self.threads = []
        self.events = []

    def record(self, operation, **fields):
        self.events.append({"operation": operation, "pid": os.getpid(),
                            "threadId": threading.get_native_id(), "at": stamp(), **fields})

    def new_socket(self, kind):
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, kind)
        sock.settimeout(3)
        self.sockets.append(sock)
        self.record("socket", fd=sock.fileno(), family="AF_INET", kind=int(kind))
        return sock

    def receive(self, sock, count, actor, flags=0):
        fd = sock.fileno()
        started = stamp()
        try:
            data, ancillary, returned, peer = sock.recvmsg(count, 0, flags)
        except TimeoutError:
            self.record("receive-timeout", actor=actor, fd=fd, requestedBytes=count,
                        requestedFlags=flags, startedAt=started)
            return None
        assert ancillary == []
        row = {"actor": actor, "fd": fd, "requestedBytes": count,
               "requestedFlags": flags, "returnedFlags": returned,
               "truncated": bool(returned & socket.MSG_TRUNC),
               "dataHex": data.hex(), "peer": peer, "startedAt": started}
        self.record("recvmsg", **row)
        return row

    def send(self, sock, data, actor, peer=None):
        fd = sock.fileno()
        if peer is None:
            sock.sendall(data)
            self.record("sendall", actor=actor, fd=fd, dataHex=data.hex())
        else:
            sent = sock.sendto(data, peer)
            assert sent == len(data)
            self.record("sendto", actor=actor, fd=fd, dataHex=data.hex(), bytesSent=sent, peer=peer)

    def close(self):
        for sock in self.sockets:
            fd = sock.fileno()
            if fd >= 0:
                try:
                    sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
                except OSError:
                    pass
                sock.close()
                self.record("close", fd=fd)
        for thread in self.threads:
            thread.join(timeout=5)
        assert all(sock.fileno() == -1 for sock in self.sockets)
        assert all(not thread.is_alive() for thread in self.threads)


def tcp_framing(experiment, case, alternate):
    messages = ["changed first record", "lamp \u2713", "third record"] if alternate else ["north route", "lamp \u2713"]
    payloads = [message.encode("utf8") for message in messages]
    wire = b"".join(struct.pack("!I", len(data)) + data for data in payloads)
    server = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    server.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    server.listen(1)
    endpoint = server.getsockname()
    experiment.record("listen", fd=server.fileno(), local=endpoint)
    first_sent, first_read = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    errors = []

    def peer():
        try:
            accepted, remote = server.accept()
            accepted.settimeout(3)
            experiment.sockets.append(accepted)
            experiment.record("accept", fd=accepted.fileno(), local=accepted.getsockname(), peer=remote)
            experiment.send(accepted, wire[:1], "server-header-fragment")
            first_sent.set()
            assert first_read.wait(timeout=3), "Client did not acknowledge its first read"
            experiment.send(accepted, wire[1:], "server-remainder")
            accepted.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
            experiment.record("shutdown-write", fd=accepted.fileno())
        except (OSError, ValueError, AssertionError, struct.error) as error:
            errors.append(type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error))
            first_sent.set()

    thread = threading.Thread(target=peer, name="owned-loopback-framing-peer")
    experiment.threads.append(thread)
    thread.start()
    client = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    client.connect(endpoint)
    experiment.record("connect", fd=client.fileno(), local=client.getsockname(), peer=client.getpeername())
    assert first_sent.wait(timeout=3), "Owned peer did not send its first fragment"
    first = experiment.receive(client, 2, "client-first-read")
    assert first is not None and bytes.fromhex(first["dataHex"]) == wire[:1]
    first_read.set()
    reads = [first]
    while True:
        row = experiment.receive(client, 3 if alternate else 2, "client-remaining-read")
        assert row is not None, "Owned stream read timed out"
        reads.append(row)
        if row["dataHex"] == "":
            break
    thread.join(timeout=5)
    assert not thread.is_alive() and not errors, errors
    observed = b"".join(bytes.fromhex(row["dataHex"]) for row in reads)
    assert observed == wire
    application_input = bytes.fromhex(first["dataHex"]) if case["framing"] == "single-read" else observed
    decoded, offset, error = [], 0, None
    while offset < len(application_input):
        if len(application_input) - offset < 4:
            error = "incomplete-length-prefix"
            break
        size = struct.unpack("!I", application_input[offset:offset + 4])[0]
        offset += 4
        if not 1 <= size <= 128:
            error = "invalid-record-length"
            break
        if len(application_input) - offset < size:
            error = "incomplete-record-body"
            break
        decoded.append(application_input[offset:offset + size].decode("utf8"))
        offset += size
    return {"messages": messages, "payloadByteLengths": [len(data) for data in payloads],
            "wireHex": wire.hex(), "firstReadHex": first["dataHex"], "readCalls": reads,
            "applicationInputHex": application_input.hex(), "applicationRecords": decoded,
            "applicationError": error, "eofObserved": reads[-1]["dataHex"] == "",
            "serverEndpoint": endpoint, "serverThreadId": thread.native_id,
            "completed": error is None and decoded == messages,
            "claimScope": "Application framing over one owned IPv4 loopback TCP stream; no packet boundaries inferred"}


def udp_probe(experiment, case, alternate):
    messages = ["changed first datagram", "second changed", "third changed"] if alternate else ["first datagram", "second datagram"]
    payloads = [message.encode("utf8") for message in messages]
    receiver = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sender = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    receiver.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    sender.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    destination, origin = receiver.getsockname(), sender.getsockname()
    experiment.record("bind", actor="receiver", fd=receiver.fileno(), local=destination)
    experiment.record("bind", actor="sender", fd=sender.fileno(), local=origin)
    for payload in payloads:
        experiment.send(sender, payload, "owned-sender", destination)
    flags = socket.MSG_PEEK if case["probe_behavior"] == "peek" else 0
    probe = experiment.receive(receiver, 4, "diagnostic-probe", flags)
    assert probe is not None and probe["peer"] == origin
    assert probe["dataHex"] == payloads[0][:4].hex() and probe["truncated"]
    receiver.settimeout(0.15)
    consumed = []
    for _ in payloads:
        row = experiment.receive(receiver, 256, "application-consumer")
        if row is not None:
            assert row["peer"] == origin and not row["truncated"]
            consumed.append(row)
    records = [bytes.fromhex(row["dataHex"]).decode("utf8") for row in consumed]
    return {"messages": messages, "sentHex": [data.hex() for data in payloads],
            "receiverEndpoint": destination, "senderEndpoint": origin,
            "probe": probe, "consumerReads": consumed, "applicationRecords": records,
            "completed": records == messages,
            "claimScope": "One owned IPv4 loopback UDP queue and its consuming or peeking application calls; no remote loss inferred"}


def run(mode):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--case", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).with_name("case.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--alternate", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if sys.platform != "linux" or sys.version_info < (3, 10) or os.getuid() == 0:
        parser.error("Use Python 3.10+ as an ordinary non-root user in an owned Linux environment")
    try:
        case_bytes = args.case.read_bytes()
        case = json.loads(case_bytes)
        expected = {"framing"} if mode == "tcp" else {"probe_behavior"}
        allowed = {"single-read", "length-prefix"} if mode == "tcp" else {"consume", "peek"}
        if not isinstance(case, dict) or set(case) != expected or not all(isinstance(value, str) and value in allowed for value in case.values()):
            raise ValueError("Case must contain only the selected investigation's documented setting")
        before, hashes, started = identity(), source_hashes(), stamp()
        out = args.report.open("x")
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        parser.error(str(error))
    experiment = Experiment()
    report = {"event": "owned-transport-investigation", "mode": mode, "case": case,
              "casePath": str(args.case.resolve()), "caseFileSha256": hashlib.sha256(case_bytes).hexdigest(),
              "alternate": args.alternate, "parentBefore": before, "sourceFileHashes": hashes,
              "startedAt": started, "notebookCompletionNotInferred": True,
              "command": [sys.executable, *sys.argv], "completed": False}
    outcome = 2
    started_clock = time.monotonic()
    try:
        observation = tcp_framing(experiment, case, args.alternate) if mode == "tcp" else udp_probe(experiment, case, args.alternate)
        report.update(observation=observation, completed=observation["completed"])
        outcome = 0 if report["completed"] else 78
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, OSError, ValueError, AssertionError, struct.error) as error:
        report["error"] = type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error)
        outcome = 130 if isinstance(error, KeyboardInterrupt) else 2
    finally:
        experiment.close()
        report.update(events=experiment.events, parentAfter=identity(),
                      allSocketsClosed=True, allThreadsJoined=True,
                      sourceUnchanged=source_hashes() == hashes,
                      endedAt=stamp(), elapsedSeconds=time.monotonic() - started_clock)
        report["parentUnchanged"] = before == report["parentAfter"]
        report["exitCode"] = outcome
        with out:
            json.dump(report, out, indent=2)
            out.write("\n")
    assert report["parentUnchanged"] and report["sourceUnchanged"]
    print(json.dumps({"report": str(args.report), "mode": mode, "completed": report["completed"],
                      "exitCode": outcome, "notebookCompletionNotInferred": True}))
    return outcome

starter/edge-cases.md.content:
# Framing reasoning cases

For each case name the application boundary, evidence needed and appropriate decoder response. The provided trial exercises valid records with a deliberately partial first observation.

1. One received byte of a four-byte length prefix.
2. A complete advertised length with an incomplete payload at EOF.
3. Two complete records in one observed byte sequence.
4. A UTF-8 payload whose byte length differs from its visible character count.
5. A claimed size over the documented 128-byte bound.
6. A long-lived connection with a complete record before EOF.

Do not label the number of socket reads as a packet count. Distinguish reasoning cases from malformed inputs actually run.

README.md.content:
# Optional extension: observe a datagram without consuming it

This optional Network Stack extension follows the required transport project.
The required project compares stream and datagram observations. This extension
investigates a diagnostic that changes the receive queue it is trying to
inspect. Preserve complete application datagrams while observing the prefix
of the next queued datagram.

The deliverable is a case configuration, a queue-state explanation, and an
evidence notebook. The prewritten apparatus runs unchanged. Programming is
optional. A working reference configuration is a comparison after an
independent attempt, not a completed explanation.

## Environment and scope

Use an ordinary non-root account in an owned Linux environment with Python 3.10
or newer. In the same terminal check `uname -s`, `hostname`, `pwd`, and
`python3 --version`. On macOS use an owned Linux lab through Remote SSH or a
Linux VM. On Windows use the Linux terminal in WSL. The apparatus creates no
remote login and refuses unsupported or root execution.

The two roles contain `main.py`, `transport_lab.py`, `case.json`,
`network-notes.md`, and `edge-cases.md`, with one shared README. Work in
`starter/` first. The only completion edit for this investigation is the
documented setting in `case.json`; leave the source apparatus unchanged.

The sender and receiver bind to operating-system-selected ports on
`127.0.0.1`. They exchange only this trial's datagrams in the current Linux
network namespace and close all their sockets afterward. The experiment
changes no routes, firewall, DNS configuration, or services. This controlled
local queue does not establish internet UDP reliability or remote reachability.

## Read the queue model

UDP preserves datagram boundaries. A consuming receive removes the next
datagram from this socket's queue. If the provided buffer is too short, Linux
can return only its prefix and mark truncation; the next consuming receive
does not supply the missing suffix. See the primary
[Linux UDP manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/udp.7.html).

The `MSG_PEEK` receive flag lets an application inspect queued data while
leaving it available for a later consuming receive. A short peek can still
report truncation of that observation. The original datagram remains queued;
a later sufficiently large consuming receive can obtain it. This is the
documented [Linux receive interface](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/recv.2.html),
exposed by [Python's socket API](https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/socket.html).

The apparatus sends two named datagrams, then performs a four-byte diagnostic
receive before the application consumer runs. The consumer uses a large
enough buffer and attempts one receive for each sent datagram. The starter
diagnostic consumes the first datagram, so the consumer starts with the second
and its last bounded receive times out. That missing consumer record is not
evidence of network loss: the earlier diagnostic already received its prefix.

The corrected diagnostic peeks. Its prefix observation is still truncated,
but the consumer subsequently receives both complete datagrams in order.
Distinguish the diagnostic's requested flags, the kernel's returned flags,
the bytes observed by each reader, and the state of the owned receive queue.

## Predict and retain the first trial

Draw this initial queue using the message names in the supplied case:

    [first complete datagram] [second complete datagram]

Predict the queue after a four-byte diagnostic read and after each subsequent
application receive. A receive buffer limits the returned payload; it does
not convert one datagram into a sequence of application messages.

From `starter/` run:

    python3 main.py --report udp-first.json

Choose a new report filename for every attempt. Exit status 78 means the
observed application records do not meet the goal. Retain this report; it is
the evidence needed to explain the failure.

Inspect `probe.dataHex`, `probe.requestedFlags`, `probe.returnedFlags`,
`probe.truncated`, `consumerReads`, and `applicationRecords`. Match the actual
sender and receiver endpoints. The report's event list also includes the
bounded receive timeout, process ID and actual native thread IDs. Do not
replace the observations with an expected transcript.

## Correct one boundary and transfer the reasoning

Change only `probe_behavior` in `case.json` to select a peeking diagnostic.
Before running, predict both the short diagnostic result and the complete
consumer results. Then run:

    python3 main.py --report udp-peek.json

The diagnostic can remain truncated while the application contract succeeds.
Explain how the two facts can both be true, using the requested receive flag
and subsequent complete payload. A different failure would require different
evidence; changing a label in the notebook does not change the queue.

Next predict the alternate trial, which sends three different datagrams, and
run:

    python3 main.py --alternate --report udp-alternate.json

Compare the new payload bytes and message count with the same queue model.
Describe why a diagnostic that consumed just one message would still be
incorrect even if later messages were received successfully.

Exit status zero checks this bounded apparatus's application contract. It
does not fill the notebook or demonstrate a remote service's availability.
Record predictions, commands, report names, the configuration change, the
actual kernel flag evidence, and the remaining scope limitation in
`network-notes.md`. Use `edge-cases.md` for the reasoning cases.

## Optional syscall evidence and recovery

If `strace` is installed in the selected Linux lab, retain a separate trial:

    strace -f -yy -s 4096 -e trace=network,close -o udp-syscalls.txt python3 main.py --report udp-traced.json

Find the probe's `recvmsg` request and distinguish its requested `MSG_PEEK`
flag from the returned truncation flag. Match subsequent consuming receives
to the original payload bytes and owned socket endpoints. A syscall trace is
evidence about these application/kernel calls, not a packet capture or a
measurement of a remote path.

Existing report filenames and invalid configuration are refused. A local
socket restriction or timeout during a failed trial needs its actual report;
it does not by itself identify a firewall, route or DNS fault. Socket deadlines
and explicit cleanup bound the owned experiment. Preserve failed evidence,
correct the local environment or selected case, and choose a fresh report
filename for recovery.

## Independent and paced checkpoints

Independently, finish the queue prediction, consuming baseline, peeking
correction, alternate trial and explanation before consulting `solution/`.
In a paced session pause after the first diagnostic observation and ask which
operation removed the message. Resume the same optional attempt and notebook.
The TCP transfer has its own question about application record boundaries;
neither optional activity replaces the required transport project.

"""Owned Linux loopback observations for two optional transport investigations."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import socket
import struct
import sys
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path


def stamp():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()  # noqa: UP017


def source_hashes():
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    return {name: hashlib.sha256((root / name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            for name in ["main.py", "transport_lab.py", "case.json", "network-notes.md", "edge-cases.md"]}


def identity():
    return {"pid": os.getpid(), "uid": os.getuid(), "hostname": socket.gethostname(),
            "cwd": str(Path.cwd()), "networkNamespace": os.readlink("/proc/self/ns/net"),
            "mountNamespace": os.readlink("/proc/self/ns/mnt")}


class Experiment:
    def __init__(self):
        self.sockets = []
        self.threads = []
        self.events = []

    def record(self, operation, **fields):
        self.events.append({"operation": operation, "pid": os.getpid(),
                            "threadId": threading.get_native_id(), "at": stamp(), **fields})

    def new_socket(self, kind):
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, kind)
        sock.settimeout(3)
        self.sockets.append(sock)
        self.record("socket", fd=sock.fileno(), family="AF_INET", kind=int(kind))
        return sock

    def receive(self, sock, count, actor, flags=0):
        fd = sock.fileno()
        started = stamp()
        try:
            data, ancillary, returned, peer = sock.recvmsg(count, 0, flags)
        except TimeoutError:
            self.record("receive-timeout", actor=actor, fd=fd, requestedBytes=count,
                        requestedFlags=flags, startedAt=started)
            return None
        assert ancillary == []
        row = {"actor": actor, "fd": fd, "requestedBytes": count,
               "requestedFlags": flags, "returnedFlags": returned,
               "truncated": bool(returned & socket.MSG_TRUNC),
               "dataHex": data.hex(), "peer": peer, "startedAt": started}
        self.record("recvmsg", **row)
        return row

    def send(self, sock, data, actor, peer=None):
        fd = sock.fileno()
        if peer is None:
            sock.sendall(data)
            self.record("sendall", actor=actor, fd=fd, dataHex=data.hex())
        else:
            sent = sock.sendto(data, peer)
            assert sent == len(data)
            self.record("sendto", actor=actor, fd=fd, dataHex=data.hex(), bytesSent=sent, peer=peer)

    def close(self):
        for sock in self.sockets:
            fd = sock.fileno()
            if fd >= 0:
                try:
                    sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
                except OSError:
                    pass
                sock.close()
                self.record("close", fd=fd)
        for thread in self.threads:
            thread.join(timeout=5)
        assert all(sock.fileno() == -1 for sock in self.sockets)
        assert all(not thread.is_alive() for thread in self.threads)


def tcp_framing(experiment, case, alternate):
    messages = ["changed first record", "lamp \u2713", "third record"] if alternate else ["north route", "lamp \u2713"]
    payloads = [message.encode("utf8") for message in messages]
    wire = b"".join(struct.pack("!I", len(data)) + data for data in payloads)
    server = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    server.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    server.listen(1)
    endpoint = server.getsockname()
    experiment.record("listen", fd=server.fileno(), local=endpoint)
    first_sent, first_read = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    errors = []

    def peer():
        try:
            accepted, remote = server.accept()
            accepted.settimeout(3)
            experiment.sockets.append(accepted)
            experiment.record("accept", fd=accepted.fileno(), local=accepted.getsockname(), peer=remote)
            experiment.send(accepted, wire[:1], "server-header-fragment")
            first_sent.set()
            assert first_read.wait(timeout=3), "Client did not acknowledge its first read"
            experiment.send(accepted, wire[1:], "server-remainder")
            accepted.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
            experiment.record("shutdown-write", fd=accepted.fileno())
        except (OSError, ValueError, AssertionError, struct.error) as error:
            errors.append(type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error))
            first_sent.set()

    thread = threading.Thread(target=peer, name="owned-loopback-framing-peer")
    experiment.threads.append(thread)
    thread.start()
    client = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    client.connect(endpoint)
    experiment.record("connect", fd=client.fileno(), local=client.getsockname(), peer=client.getpeername())
    assert first_sent.wait(timeout=3), "Owned peer did not send its first fragment"
    first = experiment.receive(client, 2, "client-first-read")
    assert first is not None and bytes.fromhex(first["dataHex"]) == wire[:1]
    first_read.set()
    reads = [first]
    while True:
        row = experiment.receive(client, 3 if alternate else 2, "client-remaining-read")
        assert row is not None, "Owned stream read timed out"
        reads.append(row)
        if row["dataHex"] == "":
            break
    thread.join(timeout=5)
    assert not thread.is_alive() and not errors, errors
    observed = b"".join(bytes.fromhex(row["dataHex"]) for row in reads)
    assert observed == wire
    application_input = bytes.fromhex(first["dataHex"]) if case["framing"] == "single-read" else observed
    decoded, offset, error = [], 0, None
    while offset < len(application_input):
        if len(application_input) - offset < 4:
            error = "incomplete-length-prefix"
            break
        size = struct.unpack("!I", application_input[offset:offset + 4])[0]
        offset += 4
        if not 1 <= size <= 128:
            error = "invalid-record-length"
            break
        if len(application_input) - offset < size:
            error = "incomplete-record-body"
            break
        decoded.append(application_input[offset:offset + size].decode("utf8"))
        offset += size
    return {"messages": messages, "payloadByteLengths": [len(data) for data in payloads],
            "wireHex": wire.hex(), "firstReadHex": first["dataHex"], "readCalls": reads,
            "applicationInputHex": application_input.hex(), "applicationRecords": decoded,
            "applicationError": error, "eofObserved": reads[-1]["dataHex"] == "",
            "serverEndpoint": endpoint, "serverThreadId": thread.native_id,
            "completed": error is None and decoded == messages,
            "claimScope": "Application framing over one owned IPv4 loopback TCP stream; no packet boundaries inferred"}


def udp_probe(experiment, case, alternate):
    messages = ["changed first datagram", "second changed", "third changed"] if alternate else ["first datagram", "second datagram"]
    payloads = [message.encode("utf8") for message in messages]
    receiver = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sender = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    receiver.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    sender.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    destination, origin = receiver.getsockname(), sender.getsockname()
    experiment.record("bind", actor="receiver", fd=receiver.fileno(), local=destination)
    experiment.record("bind", actor="sender", fd=sender.fileno(), local=origin)
    for payload in payloads:
        experiment.send(sender, payload, "owned-sender", destination)
    flags = socket.MSG_PEEK if case["probe_behavior"] == "peek" else 0
    probe = experiment.receive(receiver, 4, "diagnostic-probe", flags)
    assert probe is not None and probe["peer"] == origin
    assert probe["dataHex"] == payloads[0][:4].hex() and probe["truncated"]
    receiver.settimeout(0.15)
    consumed = []
    for _ in payloads:
        row = experiment.receive(receiver, 256, "application-consumer")
        if row is not None:
            assert row["peer"] == origin and not row["truncated"]
            consumed.append(row)
    records = [bytes.fromhex(row["dataHex"]).decode("utf8") for row in consumed]
    return {"messages": messages, "sentHex": [data.hex() for data in payloads],
            "receiverEndpoint": destination, "senderEndpoint": origin,
            "probe": probe, "consumerReads": consumed, "applicationRecords": records,
            "completed": records == messages,
            "claimScope": "One owned IPv4 loopback UDP queue and its consuming or peeking application calls; no remote loss inferred"}


def run(mode):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--case", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).with_name("case.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--alternate", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if sys.platform != "linux" or sys.version_info < (3, 10) or os.getuid() == 0:
        parser.error("Use Python 3.10+ as an ordinary non-root user in an owned Linux environment")
    try:
        case_bytes = args.case.read_bytes()
        case = json.loads(case_bytes)
        expected = {"framing"} if mode == "tcp" else {"probe_behavior"}
        allowed = {"single-read", "length-prefix"} if mode == "tcp" else {"consume", "peek"}
        if not isinstance(case, dict) or set(case) != expected or not all(isinstance(value, str) and value in allowed for value in case.values()):
            raise ValueError("Case must contain only the selected investigation's documented setting")
        before, hashes, started = identity(), source_hashes(), stamp()
        out = args.report.open("x")
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        parser.error(str(error))
    experiment = Experiment()
    report = {"event": "owned-transport-investigation", "mode": mode, "case": case,
              "casePath": str(args.case.resolve()), "caseFileSha256": hashlib.sha256(case_bytes).hexdigest(),
              "alternate": args.alternate, "parentBefore": before, "sourceFileHashes": hashes,
              "startedAt": started, "notebookCompletionNotInferred": True,
              "command": [sys.executable, *sys.argv], "completed": False}
    outcome = 2
    started_clock = time.monotonic()
    try:
        observation = tcp_framing(experiment, case, args.alternate) if mode == "tcp" else udp_probe(experiment, case, args.alternate)
        report.update(observation=observation, completed=observation["completed"])
        outcome = 0 if report["completed"] else 78
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, OSError, ValueError, AssertionError, struct.error) as error:
        report["error"] = type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error)
        outcome = 130 if isinstance(error, KeyboardInterrupt) else 2
    finally:
        experiment.close()
        report.update(events=experiment.events, parentAfter=identity(),
                      allSocketsClosed=True, allThreadsJoined=True,
                      sourceUnchanged=source_hashes() == hashes,
                      endedAt=stamp(), elapsedSeconds=time.monotonic() - started_clock)
        report["parentUnchanged"] = before == report["parentAfter"]
        report["exitCode"] = outcome

                self.record("close", fd=fd)
        for thread in self.threads:
            thread.join(timeout=5)
        assert all(sock.fileno() == -1 for sock in self.sockets)
        assert all(not thread.is_alive() for thread in self.threads)


def tcp_framing(experiment, case, alternate):
    messages = ["changed first record", "lamp \u2713", "third record"] if alternate else ["north route", "lamp \u2713"]
    payloads = [message.encode("utf8") for message in messages]
    wire = b"".join(struct.pack("!I", len(data)) + data for data in payloads)
    server = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    server.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    server.listen(1)
    endpoint = server.getsockname()
    experiment.record("listen", fd=server.fileno(), local=endpoint)
    first_sent, first_read = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    errors = []

    def peer():
        try:
            accepted, remote = server.accept()
            accepted.settimeout(3)
            experiment.sockets.append(accepted)
            experiment.record("accept", fd=accepted.fileno(), local=accepted.getsockname(), peer=remote)
            experiment.send(accepted, wire[:1], "server-header-fragment")
            first_sent.set()
            assert first_read.wait(timeout=3), "Client did not acknowledge its first read"
            experiment.send(accepted, wire[1:], "server-remainder")
            accepted.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
            experiment.record("shutdown-write", fd=accepted.fileno())
        except (OSError, ValueError, AssertionError, struct.error) as error:
            errors.append(type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error))
            first_sent.set()

    thread = threading.Thread(target=peer, name="owned-loopback-framing-peer")
    experiment.threads.append(thread)
    thread.start()
    client = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    client.connect(endpoint)
    experiment.record("connect", fd=client.fileno(), local=client.getsockname(), peer=client.getpeername())
    assert first_sent.wait(timeout=3), "Owned peer did not send its first fragment"
    first = experiment.receive(client, 2, "client-first-read")
    assert first is not None and bytes.fromhex(first["dataHex"]) == wire[:1]
    first_read.set()
    reads = [first]
    while True:
        row = experiment.receive(client, 3 if alternate else 2, "client-remaining-read")
        assert row is not None, "Owned stream read timed out"
        reads.append(row)
        if row["dataHex"] == "":
            break
    thread.join(timeout=5)
    assert not thread.is_alive() and not errors, errors
    observed = b"".join(bytes.fromhex(row["dataHex"]) for row in reads)
    assert observed == wire
    application_input = bytes.fromhex(first["dataHex"]) if case["framing"] == "single-read" else observed
    decoded, offset, error = [], 0, None
    while offset < len(application_input):
        if len(application_input) - offset < 4:
            error = "incomplete-length-prefix"
            break
        size = struct.unpack("!I", application_input[offset:offset + 4])[0]
        offset += 4
        if not 1 <= size <= 128:
            error = "invalid-record-length"
            break
        if len(application_input) - offset < size:
            error = "incomplete-record-body"
            break
        decoded.append(application_input[offset:offset + size].decode("utf8"))
        offset += size
    return {"messages": messages, "payloadByteLengths": [len(data) for data in payloads],
            "wireHex": wire.hex(), "firstReadHex": first["dataHex"], "readCalls": reads,
            "applicationInputHex": application_input.hex(), "applicationRecords": decoded,
            "applicationError": error, "eofObserved": reads[-1]["dataHex"] == "",
            "serverEndpoint": endpoint, "serverThreadId": thread.native_id,
            "completed": error is None and decoded == messages,
            "claimScope": "Application framing over one owned IPv4 loopback TCP stream; no packet boundaries inferred"}


def udp_probe(experiment, case, alternate):
    messages = ["changed first datagram", "second changed", "third changed"] if alternate else ["first datagram", "second datagram"]
    payloads = [message.encode("utf8") for message in messages]
    receiver = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    sender = experiment.new_socket(socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    receiver.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    sender.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    destination, origin = receiver.getsockname(), sender.getsockname()
    experiment.record("bind", actor="receiver", fd=receiver.fileno(), local=destination)
    experiment.record("bind", actor="sender", fd=sender.fileno(), local=origin)
    for payload in payloads:
        experiment.send(sender, payload, "owned-sender", destination)
    flags = socket.MSG_PEEK if case["probe_behavior"] == "peek" else 0
    probe = experiment.receive(receiver, 4, "diagnostic-probe", flags)
    assert probe is not None and probe["peer"] == origin
    assert probe["dataHex"] == payloads[0][:4].hex() and probe["truncated"]
    receiver.settimeout(0.15)
    consumed = []
    for _ in payloads:
        row = experiment.receive(receiver, 256, "application-consumer")
        if row is not None:
            assert row["peer"] == origin and not row["truncated"]
            consumed.append(row)
    records = [bytes.fromhex(row["dataHex"]).decode("utf8") for row in consumed]
    return {"messages": messages, "sentHex": [data.hex() for data in payloads],
            "receiverEndpoint": destination, "senderEndpoint": origin,
            "probe": probe, "consumerReads": consumed, "applicationRecords": records,
            "completed": records == messages,
            "claimScope": "One owned IPv4 loopback UDP queue and its consuming or peeking application calls; no remote loss inferred"}


def run(mode):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--case", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).with_name("case.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--report", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--alternate", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if sys.platform != "linux" or sys.version_info < (3, 10) or os.getuid() == 0:
        parser.error("Use Python 3.10+ as an ordinary non-root user in an owned Linux environment")
    try:
        case_bytes = args.case.read_bytes()
        case = json.loads(case_bytes)
        expected = {"framing"} if mode == "tcp" else {"probe_behavior"}
        allowed = {"single-read", "length-prefix"} if mode == "tcp" else {"consume", "peek"}
        if not isinstance(case, dict) or set(case) != expected or not all(isinstance(value, str) and value in allowed for value in case.values()):
            raise ValueError("Case must contain only the selected investigation's documented setting")
        before, hashes, started = identity(), source_hashes(), stamp()
        out = args.report.open("x")
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        parser.error(str(error))
    experiment = Experiment()
    report = {"event": "owned-transport-investigation", "mode": mode, "case": case,
              "casePath": str(args.case.resolve()), "caseFileSha256": hashlib.sha256(case_bytes).hexdigest(),
              "alternate": args.alternate, "parentBefore": before, "sourceFileHashes": hashes,
              "startedAt": started, "notebookCompletionNotInferred": True,
              "command": [sys.executable, *sys.argv], "completed": False}
    outcome = 2
    started_clock = time.monotonic()
    try:
        observation = tcp_framing(experiment, case, args.alternate) if mode == "tcp" else udp_probe(experiment, case, args.alternate)
        report.update(observation=observation, completed=observation["completed"])
        outcome = 0 if report["completed"] else 78
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, OSError, ValueError, AssertionError, struct.error) as error:
        report["error"] = type(error).__name__ + ": " + str(error)
        outcome = 130 if isinstance(error, KeyboardInterrupt) else 2
    finally:
        experiment.close()
        report.update(events=experiment.events, parentAfter=identity(),
                      allSocketsClosed=True, allThreadsJoined=True,
                      sourceUnchanged=source_hashes() == hashes,
                      endedAt=stamp(), elapsedSeconds=time.monotonic() - started_clock)
        report["parentUnchanged"] = before == report["parentAfter"]
        report["exitCode"] = outcome
        with out:
            json.dump(report, out, indent=2)
            out.write("\n")
    assert report["parentUnchanged"] and report["sourceUnchanged"]
    print(json.dumps({"report": str(args.report), "mode": mode, "completed": report["completed"],
                      "exitCode": outcome, "notebookCompletionNotInferred": True}))
    return outcome

# Queue reasoning cases

Draw the owned receive queue and name the operation responsible for each state.

1. A short consuming diagnostic before the application consumer.
2. A short MSG_PEEK diagnostic before a sufficiently large consuming read.
3. Requested MSG_PEEK versus returned MSG_TRUNC.
4. Three sent datagrams with one consumed by a diagnostic.
5. A bounded empty-queue timeout after earlier successful receives.
6. A second consumer racing this diagnostic: explain why this controlled one-consumer trial does not prove concurrent behavior.

A missing consumer record does not establish network loss when another local receive already consumed that datagram.
